0.long_answer: The most common benign tumor of the adrenal glands linked to abnormal cAMP-dependent protein kinase A signaling is the cortisol-producing adrenocortical adenoma. These adenomas are frequently associated with Cushing syndrome and have been found to harbor somatic mutations in the PRKACA gene, which codes for the catalytic subunit of PKA. This mutation leads to constitutive activation of the cAMP/PKA pathway, driving excess cortisol production and tumor development. Thus, the majority of benign cortisol-producing lesions in the adrenal cortex are attributable to alterations in this signaling pathway.
